short_description: A chest-focused pressing movement that works the pectorals and front shoulders through a valley-shaped arm path.
how_to: Stand or sit with a dumbbell in each hand at chest height.
Press the weights together in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest at the top of the movement.
Lower the weights slowly back to the start.
Repeat with controlled presses.
correct: Move with a slow, controlled tempo.
Keep your shoulders down and back.
mistakes: Don't rush the press.
Don't shrug your shoulders up.
Don't let the weights drift apart at the top.
Don't arch your lower back excessively.

short_description: A half-bent push-forward movement that engages the upper back and shoulders through a horizontal pressing action.
how_to: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hinge slightly at the hips.
Hold your arms bent at your sides.
Push both arms forward at shoulder height.
Pull them back to the start with control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Move your arms at a steady pace.
Keep a slight bend in your knees.
mistakes: Don't round your upper back.
Don't lock your knees.
Don't swing your torso to add momentum.
Don't let your shoulders creep up.

short_description: A dumbbell upright row that targets the upper traps and lateral deltoids by pulling the weights vertically.
how_to: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Pull the dumbbells straight up close to your body.
Lead with your elbows until they reach shoulder height.
Lower the weights slowly back to the start.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Keep the dumbbells close to your body.
Keep your elbows higher than your wrists.
mistakes: Don't jerk the weights up.
Don't pull the dumbbells higher than your chin.
Don't lean back as you lift.
Don't let your wrists lead the movement.

short_description: A bent-over dumbbell row that strengthens the upper and mid back by pulling the weights toward your torso.
how_to: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang below your chest.
Pull both weights up toward your ribcage, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the dumbbells slowly and repeat.
correct: Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
mistakes: Don't round your lower back.
Don't jerk the weights up.
Don't let your elbows flare out wide.
Don't lift your torso to assist the row.

short_description: A dumbbell kickback that isolates the triceps by extending the arm backward from a hinged position.
how_to: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hinge forward at the hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your upper arms tucked against your sides.
Extend both arms straight back, squeezing the triceps.
Slowly return to the bent position.
Repeat without swinging.
correct: Keep your upper arms still throughout.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension.
mistakes: Don't swing your arms to build momentum.
Don't round your back.
Don't drop your elbows during the movement.
Don't use a weight too heavy to control.

short_description: A dumbbell donkey kick that targets the glutes by driving one leg back and up against added resistance.
how_to: Start on all fours with a dumbbell tucked behind one knee.
Keep your core tight and your back flat.
Drive that leg back and up until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch legs.
correct: Squeeze your glute at the top.
mistakes: Don't arch your lower back.
Don't let your hips rotate open.
Don't swing the leg for momentum.
Don't rush the movement.

short_description: A dumbbell backward lunge that works the quads, glutes and hamstrings while adding load with dumbbells.
how_to: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your knees over your toes.
Keep your heels down on the front foot.
mistakes: Don't let your knees cave inward.
Don't drop too fast.
Don't let your front knee push past your toes.
Don't lean your torso forward.

short_description: A single-leg deadlift that challenges hamstring strength and balance by hinging on one leg.
how_to: Stand on one leg with a soft bend in the knee.
Hinge forward at the hips while raising your free leg behind you.
Lower your hands toward the floor while keeping your back flat.
Return to standing by driving your hips forward.
Complete your reps then switch legs.
correct: Keep your back flat throughout the hinge.
Keep your hips square to the floor.
mistakes: Don't round your lower back.
Don't let your hips rotate open.
Don't lock out your standing knee.
Don't rush the return.

short_description: A dumbbell hip thrust that builds glute strength by driving the hips up against resistance from a dumbbell.
how_to: Sit with your upper back against a bench and a dumbbell resting on your hips.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Drive your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.
correct: Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
mistakes: Don't hyperextend your lower back at the top.
Don't let your knees fall inward.
Don't bounce at the bottom.
Don't rush the movement.

short_description: A dynamic plank variation that works the core, obliques and hip flexors by drawing the knee toward the elbow.
how_to: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Bring one knee out and toward the same-side elbow.
Return the foot to the start position.
Alternate sides for the desired reps.
Keep your hips level throughout.
correct: Keep your body in one line.
Keep your hips level as you move your leg.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back sag.
Don't lift your hips too high.
Don't twist your torso as you bring the knee in.
Don't rush and lose alignment.

short_description: A dumbbell pullover that stretches and works the chest, lats and serratus by arcing the weight overhead from a lying position.
how_to: Lie on your back on a bench with both hands gripping one dumbbell above your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch.
Pull the weight back up over your chest along the same arc.
Repeat with controlled movement.
correct: Keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Move through a full but comfortable arc.
mistakes: Don't lock your elbows straight.
Don't drop the weight too fast.
Don't let your lower back arch off the bench.
Don't use momentum to swing the weight up.

short_description: A dumbbell swing that trains the posterior chain and builds power by hinging and driving the hips forward.
how_to: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one dumbbell with both hands.
Hinge at the hips and let the dumbbell swing back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the weight to shoulder height.
Let the weight swing back down as you hinge again.
Repeat in a smooth, rhythmic motion.
correct: Drive from your hips, not your arms.
Keep your heels on the floor.
mistakes: Don't squat the movement instead of hinging.
Don't round your lower back.
Don't use your arms to muscle the weight up.
Don't let the dumbbell pull you forward.

short_description: A tricep flick-back that isolates the back of the upper arm through a short, controlled extension.
how_to: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your elbows bent at your sides.
Extend your forearms back and slightly flick at the wrist at the end range.
Return to the bent position with control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your upper arms still and close to your sides.
Move only from the elbow down.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate.
mistakes: Don't swing your torso to help the movement.
Don't let your elbows drop.
Don't use a weight too heavy to control.
Don't rush the extension.

short_description: A standing knee lift that activates the hip flexors and challenges balance by raising one knee at a time.
how_to: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Shift your weight onto one foot.
Drive the opposite knee up toward your chest.
Lower your foot back down with control.
Alternate sides for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your standing leg slightly bent.
Keep your chest up and shoulders relaxed.
mistakes: Don't lean back as you lift the knee.
Don't let your standing knee collapse inward.
Don't rush between reps.
Don't hunch your shoulders.

short_description: A seated overhead tricep extension that isolates the triceps by extending a dumbbell from behind the head.
how_to: Sit upright on a bench or chair and hold one dumbbell with both hands.
Raise the dumbbell overhead and lower it behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the top, squeezing your triceps.
Keep your elbows pointing forward throughout.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your elbows close to your head.
Keep your core braced and your back upright.
Squeeze your triceps at the top.
mistakes: Don't let your elbows flare out wide.
Don't arch your lower back.
Don't use momentum to swing the weight up.
Don't lock out your elbows aggressively at the top.

short_description: A facial toning exercise that targets the jaw muscles and neck by controlled jaw and chin movements.
how_to: Sit or stand with a tall, relaxed posture.
Tilt your chin slightly upward.
Open and close your mouth in a slow, exaggerated chewing motion.
Hold the open position for a breath, then close.
Repeat for the desired reps.
mistakes: Don't strain or force the movement.
Don't tense your neck muscles unnecessarily.
Don't hold your breath.
Don't jut your chin aggressively forward.

short_description: A single-arm dumbbell triceps kickback that isolates the triceps through a controlled arm extension.
how_to: Stand with one knee and hand on a bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand with your upper arm parallel to the floor.
Extend your forearm back until your arm is straight.
Squeeze your triceps at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch arms.
correct: Keep your upper arm still and parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension.
mistakes: Don't swing your arm for momentum.
Don't let your elbow drop during the movement.
Don't round your back.
Don't use a weight you cannot fully control.

short_description: A facial and neck exercise that targets the area under the chin by drawing the head in a gentle duck motion.
how_to: Sit or stand with a tall posture and relaxed shoulders.
Gently tuck your chin toward your chest.
Push your lower jaw forward slightly in a scooping motion.
Return to the neutral position with control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
mistakes: Don't force your chin down aggressively.
Don't tense your neck muscles.
Don't hold your breath.
Don't rush the movement.

short_description: A facial toning exercise that works the muscles around the eyes through controlled upward eye movements.
how_to: Sit comfortably with your head upright and shoulders relaxed.
Place your index fingers gently under your eyebrows.
Look upward while resisting with your fingers.
Hold briefly, then relax the muscles.
Repeat for the desired reps.
correct: Keep your facial muscles relaxed except for those being targeted.
Keep your shoulders and neck relaxed.
mistakes: Don't strain or squint your eyes.
Don't press too hard with your fingers.
Don't hold your breath.
Don't tilt your head back to compensate.

short_description: A facial toning exercise that targets the muscles around the mouth and cheeks through a pursed-lip expression.
how_to: Sit or stand with a relaxed, upright posture.
Purse your lips together as if about to give a kiss.
Hold the position for a breath, then relax.
Repeat in a slow, steady rhythm.
Perform for the desired number of reps.
correct: Keep your shoulders and neck relaxed.
Keep the expression controlled and deliberate.
mistakes: Don't force or strain the expression.
Don't tense your neck muscles.
Don't hold your breath.
Don't rush through the reps.
